entries.name: Role-author-recipient-topic model
entries.definition: A family of message-content models in which actors have latent-role distributions and ordered sender-role/recipient-role pairs determine topic mixtures, with token-level or message-level role assignments.
entries.identity_notes: Scoped to the RART family introduced by McCallum and colleagues, with the 2007 preprint specifying RART1 in detail and sketching RART2 and RART3. RART1 draws both roles per token; RART2 fixes a sender role and individual recipient roles per message; RART3 uses one common recipient role per message. The latter sketches are not asserted to provide complete independent inference algorithms. Explicit actor roles distinguish this family from ART pair-specific topic vectors and author-topic models. RART is a source acronym within this scope. No normalized candidate identity matched all 442 pinned AIO IDs, labels and scoped synonyms or 429 preceding native IDs, names and aliases. Full-checkout searches included ignored and hidden files in both checkouts; 23 matching lines per checkout came from four unique file contents containing prior frontier leads and contextual distinctions. All matching excerpts were inspected. The semantic search returned 205 label/synonym hits, with 204 unchanged from prior reading and one newly read. Eighteen annotated AIO CLASS nodes and outgoing edges were byte-verified against prior inspected versions. Twenty-six contextual YAMLs comprise 24 unchanged prior readings and two final round102 records verified against their fully read scientific-review inputs. No candidate record is present within this bounded pinned-snapshot and maintained-corpus search.
limitations: Only RART1 has a detailed generative specification in this source. The RART2/3 diagrams and prose leave further implementation and inference choices for exploration; family coverage does not certify fully specified variants.

The demonstrated 15-role, 50-topic fit is illustrated by selected email users and manually named roles in Tables 6-7. Some apparently unrelated assignments remain unexplained, and entity-resolution errors are present. These examples do not establish verified occupations, expertise, causal influence or universal predictive superiority. Earlier ART perplexity results are not RART benchmark results.

Fixed role/topic counts, bag-of-words observations, uniform recipient selection and corpus-specific participation affect identifiability and interpretation. Latent role labels are exchangeable; semantic names are human interpretations. A single ART sample judged plausible does not establish adequate uncertainty propagation or convergence.

Finite synthetic collapsed-probability checks cover the specified RART1 factorization, including a shared actor in sender and recipient positions. They are not a reproduction of historical software, email preprocessing or the reported benchmark.

definition_evidence.locator: Section 5, preprint printed/PDF pp.17-19 and Figure 6 p.18

claims.statement: In RART1, each actor has a Dirichlet-distributed role vector psi, each ordered sender-role/recipient-role pair has a Dirichlet topic vector theta, and each topic has a Dirichlet word vector phi. Given observed sender a and a nonempty recipient set R, a token chooses r uniformly from R, sender role g from psi_a, recipient role h from psi_r, topic z from theta_gh, then word w from phi_z. An actor uses the same role vector for sending and receiving, while theta distinguishes the order of the roles. The model conditions on participants and message lengths rather than generating network edges. Shared random vectors must be integrated jointly across their uses; two roles drawn for the same actor need not be independent after psi is integrated out.

evidence.locator: Section 5, preprint pp.18-19, RART1 generative description and joint distribution

claims.statement: The reported RART1 experiment first fits ART, fixes topic and recipient assignments from one sample, and then infers the role structure conditionally on those assignments. This staged procedure does not sample the full joint RART posterior or propagate all uncertainty in the frozen assignments. The source states that general Gibbs updates can be derived, but its Appendix A derives ART updates, not a complete RART sampler. Conditional on fixed parameters, token role choices can vary within a message; RART2 and RART3 impose different message-level sharing and cannot be substituted without changing the model.

evidence.locator: Section 5, preprint pp.18-19; Section 6, pp.19-20; Appendix A, pp.21-22

entries.name: Multi-label text mixture model
entries.definition: A generative multi-label document model that selects a label subset and a mixture supported on that subset, then generates each word through one of the selected labels and its class-specific word distribution.
entries.identity_notes: Scoped to McCallum's 1999 mixture model for multi-label text classification, whose training observes document label sets while token labels are latent. The maintained name describes this source construction; no source acronym is invented. It differs from independent binary classifiers, mutually exclusive multiclass classification and unsupervised topic discovery. The uniform author-word comparator cited by later author-topic papers is a simplified case, not an alias for the full learned label-mixture construction. No normalized candidate identity matched all 442 pinned AIO IDs, labels and scoped synonyms or 429 preceding native IDs, names and aliases. Full-checkout searches included ignored and hidden files in both checkouts; 23 matching lines per checkout came from four unique file contents containing prior frontier leads and contextual distinctions. All matching excerpts were inspected. The semantic search returned 205 label/synonym hits, with 204 unchanged from prior reading and one newly read. Eighteen annotated AIO CLASS nodes and outgoing edges were byte-verified against prior inspected versions. Twenty-six contextual YAMLs comprise 24 unchanged prior readings and two final round102 records verified against their fully read scientific-review inputs. No candidate record is present within this bounded pinned-snapshot and maintained-corpus search.
limitations: The prior-mode substitution is not generally the integrated likelihood or the posterior mode of lambda given the document. Per-subset parameters and label-subset search become difficult with many labels; the source uses backoff and heuristic search.

The reported additive estimate (count+m)/(D+m*number_of_subsets) is a posterior mean under symmetric Dirichlet(m), or an interior MAP estimate under Dirichlet(m+1). With positive m it is not generally MAP under a flat Dirichlet(1), despite the source wording. The m=1 Laplace estimator can be retained without adopting that prior interpretation.

Experiments use Reuters-21578 ModApte and particular preprocessing; the ten-class binary naive-Bayes baseline vocabulary was selected on test data, explicitly noted by the author. Preliminary 90-label results report improved macro F1 with unchanged micro F1 and precision/recall tradeoffs. No universal advantage or modern comparative claim follows.

Background and uniform components are smoothing/modeling devices, not evidence that every document belongs to a real semantic background class. The original PostScript and converted PDF are separately hashed. No author code or benchmark was executed.

definition_evidence.locator: Section 2, converted PDF pp.2-3, generative process and Equation (1)

claims.statement: A document first chooses a label subset c with prior P(c), then a mixing vector lambda from P(lambda|c) with zero mass outside that subset. For each word, a label is sampled from lambda and the word from that label's categorical distribution. Training supplies document label subsets and leaves token-label assignments unobserved. Classifying a new document compares subset scores containing P(c) and the word likelihood integrated over lambda. The presented implementation approximates that integral by evaluating one prior-mode mixture for each subset, rather than fitting or integrating an arbitrary full mixing distribution. The source's first displayed document probability omits P(c); Equation (1) includes it consistently with the generative description.

evidence.locator: Section 2, converted PDF pp.2-3, first document-probability display and Equation (1)

claims.statement: The fitting procedure assigns posterior label responsibilities to words, pools class-word counts across documents, and pools mixture weights over documents with the same observed label subset. Unseen subsets use an overlap-weighted backoff from observed subset mixtures. The reported modifications include leave-one-document-out responsibility estimation, a shared learned background component and a uniform word component. Prediction combines two greedy searches over label subsets; annealing is suggested as another search approach. These approximations and modifications do not establish exact marginalization, globally optimal subset selection, or ordinary full-data EM monotonicity.

entries.definition: A latent-factor document model that shares each document's fixed topic proportions between categorical term and citation-incidence channels, with topic-specific distributions for each channel.
entries.identity_notes: Scoped to Cohn and Hofmann's joint content/connectivity model in The Missing Link. The maintained name describes its term/citation construction; PHITS names a link-only predecessor and is not used as an alias. Fixed document memberships distinguish this PLSA-style model from the integrated Dirichlet word/reference model of Erosheva and colleagues. limitations: The exposition alternates between citing-source and cited-target language: Section 2 defines an incidence matrix as document i cited by j, while PHITS and Section 3 use differing verbal descriptions. The factor equations apply to the chosen orientation, but transposing the matrix changes the modeling task. No unique historical implementation orientation is inferred.

The displayed channel normalization is undefined for a document with an empty channel; a complete implementation needs an explicit missing-channel policy. Alpha endpoints discard one channel. Fixed topic count, categorical incidence modeling and fixed document weights constrain generalization; unseen documents require inference of new mixtures.

The reported factor-space nearest-neighbor classification, topic counts tied to known category counts, and source-page ranking among random distractors are specific evaluation setups. They do not establish recovery of true classes, universal advantage, or a demonstrated end-to-end web crawler.

Reference-flow scores sum over observed link support and use reverse document-given-topic probabilities requiring prior and normalization choices. They are not automatically a calibrated Markov transition or causal information flow. The proposed continuous-state MDP extension is prospective. No author code or benchmark was executed.

definition_evidence.locator: Sections 2-3, PDF pp.2-4, mixture equations and joint criterion (2)

claims.statement: Each document d has one fixed topic probability vector theta_d. Topic z has a categorical term distribution phi_z and a separate categorical citation-incidence distribution psi_z. The channel mixtures are P(t|d)=sum_z theta_dz*phi_zt and P(c|d)=sum_z theta_dz*psi_zc. Topic choices are made per observation and share the document weights; the construction is not one latent topic for a whole document and does not integrate a Dirichlet membership prior. The source optimizes alpha times the term log score plus 1-alpha times the link log score, separately normalizing each document's counts in each channel. This weighted criterion gives equal document mass per nonempty channel and differs from the raw-count corpus likelihood.

evidence.locator: Section 3, PDF pp.3-4, channel mixtures and Equation (2)

claims.statement: An EM-style fit computes topic responsibilities separately for observed terms and citation incidences, then pools their document-normalized expected counts with channel weights alpha and 1-alpha. Document mixtures combine the two channel responsibility averages, and each topic's emission counts must be normalized over its own channel categories. Equation (3) has an inconsistent document subscript in its first numerator, and the displayed emission updates in Equation (4) omit the final categorical normalization; use the conditioning document and normalized vectors for a coherent probability model. Experiments use tempered responsibilities, so ordinary beta=1 EM monotonicity does not certify the whole temperature schedule.

evidence.locator: Section 3, PDF p.4, Equations (3)-(5); Section 4.1, PDF p.5, tempering settings

notes: All seven official NIPS 2000 pages visually read, including all displays and references. No numeric printed page labels visible. Often cited as 2001 publication; use exact official conference and PDF version.

Sections 2-3 pp.2-4 define a joint factor model for term and link-incidence channels sharing document-specific fixed mixing vectors P(z|d). Each topic has term and citation-ID emission probabilities. This is a fixed-membership PLSA-style model, not the integrated Dirichlet word/reference model of Erosheva et al. and not one latent class per whole document.

The fitted objective Eq.2 p.4 separately normalizes each document term/link count vector and combines their log scores with alpha and 1-alpha. Thus documents receive equal channel mass when both channels are nonempty; this is a weighted/normalized criterion, not the raw count corpus likelihood. Empty channel denominators require a policy not specified by the display. Alpha endpoints use only one channel.

Printed EM qualifications: Eq.3 first term posterior appears to use d_k instead of d_j in the numerator, while its denominator and conditioning use d_j; use the consistent conditioning document. Eq.4 emission updates show accumulated weighted responsibilities with equality but no final topic-wise normalization; normalized categorical emission vectors require it. Eq.5 mixes channel responsibilities by alpha. The experiments use tempered responsibilities, so ordinary EM likelihood monotonicity should not be asserted for the whole annealed procedure.

Link orientation is inconsistent across exposition: Section 2 defines A_ij as document i cited by j, then calls PHITS an inlink/citation-source model; Section 3 calls the row-variable probability linking to document l. The formulas model whatever incidence orientation is supplied. Do not silently equate incoming-source and outgoing-target interpretations or use a PHITS alias until inspecting its primary source.

Section 4.1 p.5 reports cosine nearest-neighbor classification in factor space, topic counts chosen to match class counts, a 15 percent test subset and particular tempering settings. It is not supervised generative training or universal advantage over PLSA/PHITS. Exact held-out content/link access protocol is not fully established from this short account.

Section 4.2 p.6 defines reference-flow scores by summing products of document-given-topic or mixture weights over observed link support. Distinguish P(d|z) from P(z|d); recovering the reverse requires document-prior and normalization choices, especially for arbitrary mixture points. The displayed sum is over nonzero links, not explicitly multiplied by link counts. No automatically calibrated transition kernel, causal flow or stationary Markov law follows.

Section 4.3 pp.6-7 evaluates ranking known source pages relative to random distractors on WebKB, not a demonstrated end-to-end web crawl. Distractors were not screened to remove true sources. A continuous-state MDP treatment is a prospective suggestion. No author implementation or benchmark was executed.

References p.7 expose PHITS (Cohn/Chang 2000), HITS, PageRank, latent semantic analysis, TextTiling and probabilistic relational models; NMF and tempered EM have existing coverage/frontier. Deduplicate before adding leads.

All 24 pages of the author-hosted 2007 preprint visually read after the round102 review cutoff. Title header says JAIR 29 (2007) with placeholder pages and September publication; official final metadata instead gives volume 30, pages 249-272 and October 13. Cite this downloaded preprint with its printed/PDF pagination, not final journal pagination. Author order is McCallum, Wang, Corrada-Emmanuel.

Sections 2-4 pp.3-17 revisit ART. Page 5 correctly integrates shared corpus parameters globally, unlike the separately integrated corpus display on the earlier 2004 report p.4. Gibbs display p.6 and Appendix A p.22 print minus-one counts; interpret as leave-one-token-out counts for candidate assignments, not blindly subtracting one from every candidate cell. The appendix derives a corpus collapsed joint, not independent document integrals. Perplexity stability does not prove mixing.

Section 5 pp.17-19 and Figure 6 p.18 distinguish three RART variants. RART1 chooses sender and recipient roles for every token. RART2 fixes one sender role and individual recipient roles for a message, then chooses the recipient role per token. RART3 uses a common recipient role for all recipients in a message. Only RART1 is specified in detail; RART2/3 are left for exploration. Retain the family identity with this explicit maturity distinction rather than asserting three fully developed algorithms.

RART1 gives each observed actor one Dirichlet role vector psi, each ordered sender-role/recipient-role pair a Dirichlet topic vector theta, and each topic a Dirichlet word vector phi. A token draws an eligible recipient uniformly, sender role from psi of observed sender, recipient role from psi of selected recipient, topic from the ordered role-pair vector, then word. The same actor-role vector is used for sending and receiving, while the topic tensor distinguishes role order. Sender, recipients and message length are conditioned on, not generated. If sender equals selected recipient, two role draws share psi; integrating it couples them.

Section 6 pp.19-20 fits a staged approximation: run ART, lock one sample of topic and recipient assignments, then fit roles. This is conditional inference given fixed assignments, not full joint RART posterior sampling. A sample judged good in the source is not sufficient to establish posterior concentration or uncertainty propagation. General RART Gibbs formulas are said derivable but not provided.

Tables 6-7 pp.19-20 show selected roles and users from a 15-role, 50-topic run. Role titles and interpretations are supplied by authors; some apparently unrelated users remain unexplained, and two user IDs are the same person. These illustrative results do not establish independently verified job roles, expertise, causal influence or universal empirical superiority. Earlier ART perplexity comparisons pp.16-17 are not RART performance evidence; they use a high overlap of train/test participant pairs and plug-in parameter estimates.

References pp.22-24 expose group-topic modeling, infinite relational models, Pachinko allocation, Topics over Time, topical n-grams and expertise/reviewer matching. Several belong to an existing author-index cohort; deduplicate explicit new leads. Classical block models and overlapping roles already have a frontier cohort. Model Section 2 pp.2-3 first selects a label subset, draws a document mixture supported on that subset, then generates each word by drawing one label and its categorical word emission. Training observes document label sets but not token labels. This differs from independent binary classification and from unsupervised document topics. The author-word endpoint described in later AT/ART papers is a simplified uniform-mixture case, not the full learned mixture construction here.

The first unnumbered document probability on p.3 omits the label-set prior despite the stated generative process. Equation 1 includes P(c) correctly. Classification integrates lambda conditional on the set in the model; the actual presented approximation substitutes one prior-mode mixture for each label set. Mode likelihood is not generally an integral or a MAP posterior over lambda, and the prose about learned mixture distributions should not imply the full distribution was fitted.

Parameter estimation p.4 uses class responsibilities for word tokens and updates per-label-set mixture weights plus global class-word laws. Lambda updates are pooled over documents with exactly the same observed label subset. Unseen label sets back off to averages of training-set mixture weights weighted by class overlap. Document class-set search uses two greedy schemes together and suggests annealing; it does not guarantee the globally most probable subset.

Additional Features p.4 performs a leave-one-document-out E-step, adds a learned background English class shared by all documents, and a uniform word component for smoothing. The modified leave-one-out iteration is not ordinary exact EM for one fixed full-data likelihood, so textbook monotonicity/global optimality should not be asserted. Background components are modeling devices, not labels proving every document is in English.

Prior/smoothing wording needs qualification: the reported (count+m)/(D+m*number_of_sets) is an additive pseudocount estimator. It is a posterior mean under symmetric Dirichlet(m), or interior MAP under Dirichlet(m+1), not generally MAP under a flat Dirichlet(1) when m is positive. The source calls this MAP with a uniform prior and m=1 Laplace smoothing; keep estimator and interpretation distinct.

Experiments pp.5-6 use Reuters-21578 ModApte and ten largest classes, particular token preprocessing and exact-set accuracy plus per-label accuracy. Binary naive-Bayes baseline vocabulary size was selected on the test set, explicitly noted by the author. Preliminary 90-label results report improved macro F1 but unchanged micro F1 and precision/recall tradeoffs. No universal superiority or comparison to modern classifiers follows. Author software and benchmark were not executed.

References pp.6-7 expose Imai et al. simultaneous-topic model, text classification shrinkage, deleted interpolation, labeled/unlabeled EM and BooTexter. Preserve already represented generic EM/PLSA/SVM identities and inspect these separate methods before curation.

limitations: The number of topics is finite and fixed in this construction. Integrating a continuous Dirichlet mixture does not introduce infinitely many topic classes. Infinite exchangeability supports the representation discussed in Section 3.1; arbitrary finite exchangeability alone is not the asserted theorem.

Given observed topic assignments, Dirichlet conjugacy is exact. With topics unobserved, the marginal posterior over proportions is generally not a single Dirichlet; gamma=alpha+expected counts is a variational update, not exact marginal conjugacy. Exact inference is generally difficult, and bound optimization need not monotonically improve the true likelihood or attain its global maximum.

The basic model ignores word order and explicit within-topic dependencies, though integrating document proportions induces dependence between tokens. Zero word probabilities require smoothing or other support handling for novel documents. A prior over document mixtures does not guarantee freedom from overfitting, identifiable topics or meaningful semantic labels.

The Bayesian topic-prior extension requires expected log topic probabilities in its assignment update. The appendix’s printed alpha Hessian has a sign/factor mismatch with the preceding gradient; the consistent Hessian is M*(trigamma(sum alpha)-delta_ij*trigamma(alpha_i)). This record does not adopt that printed Hessian as verified code. Equation (13) correctly uses the normalized posterior.

The comparison’s empirical mixture over training-document indices must weight an entire document once; the printed p(d) inside its token product is not adopted. These mathematical qualifications do not establish an error in unseen author software or experiments.

The source’s document, classification and recommendation experiments have distinct protocols. No exact likelihood replication, generic performance advantage or biological-mechanism conclusion is claimed. All source material concerns the specified 2003 model, not every later topic-model extension.

claims.statement: For a fixed K, positive alpha_i and normalized topic-word probability rows B_i, draw theta_d~Dirichlet(alpha) independently for each document. Given a document length N_d, draw z_dn~Categorical(theta_d) and w_dn~Categorical(B_zdn) for each token. Conditional on theta_d and B, token probabilities are sum_i theta_di*B_iw and tokens are independent; integrating theta_d gives p(w_d|alpha,B)=integral Dir(theta_d;alpha)*product_n(sum_i theta_di*B_i,w_dn)dtheta_d. This is an exchangeable document distribution, generally with dependent tokens after integration. An unordered count vector additionally includes its multinomial multiplicity. The paper’s Poisson length law is optional to this conditional construction. For fixed B, its mean-field approximation is q(theta,z)=Dir(theta;gamma)*product_n Cat(z_n;phi_n), with phi_ni proportional B_i,w_n*exp[digamma(gamma_i)-digamma(sum_j gamma_j)] and gamma_i=alpha_i+sum_n phi_ni. Variational EM optimizes the evidence lower bound, updating B from expected topic-word counts and alpha numerically. Section 5.4 separately places Dirichlet priors on B; then the assignment update uses expected log topic probabilities, not fixed B values.

limitations: The base construction is a normalized distribution of indexed co-occurrences. It has no LDA-style population prior on new document mixtures; fold-in estimation is possible, so this is not a claim that unseen documents cannot be represented at all.

Training-document mixture parameters grow with the corpus. Maximum-likelihood or tempered fitting can overfit; local EM optimization, initialization and rank selection do not guarantee global optimality or unique factors. Permuting topic labels preserves the law, and linearly dependent topic distributions can yield nonunique mixture weights.

The bag-of-words representation omits token order and explicit within-topic word interactions. It is not a raw-count Poisson MRF, a canonical-parameter admixture, or a neural density estimator. Topic labels and selected high-probability words are interpretations, not verified semantic or causal categories.

Positive-count cells require positive modeled mass. Responsibility updates need nonzero denominators; unused components require a specified handling convention. Zero-count terms use the standard zero-contribution convention.

Historical retrieval experiments use particular corpora, ranks, held-out tempering and cosine interpolation. No universal retrieval advantage, exact new-document marginal likelihood or author implementation is certified.

native_neighbors.name: Author-topic model
native_neighbors.definition: A generative document model in which each author has a shared topic-proportion distribution and each word is produced by uniformly selecting an author from the document's observed author set, selecting a topic from that author, and selecting a word from that topic.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: Scoped to Rosen-Zvi, Griffiths, Steyvers and Smyth's UAI 2004 author-topic model, whose arXiv deposit occurred in 2012. It conditions on a document's authors and pools topic preferences across their documents. It is distinct from document-specific LDA, a pure author-word mixture, author-recipient-topic models and personalized large language models. Latent token-author assignments are model variables, not observed intellectual contributions. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels and scoped synonyms and 423 preceding native IDs, names and aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main. Ten matched lines in each checkout reduce to nine unique line contents: prior frontier references, copied discovery context and cached web-result mentions. Every matching concept excerpt was inspected; these are not maintained or imported identities. All 200 semantic label/synonym hits were read. Eighteen exact annotated AIO CLASS nodes and outgoing edges were inspected, including 14 verified unchanged from prior reading and four newly read. Thirty contextual YAMLs comprise those 18 AIO records and 12 native neighbors: six fully read here, 23 byte-verified after prior reading and the updated APM verified against its fully reviewed round100 bytes. Absence is bounded to the pinned snapshot, maintained corpus and inspected semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Known author sets, uniform token-level author choice, fixed topic count, bag-of-words observations and stationary author preferences constrain the model. The author set is conditioned on, not generated. Coauthors with indistinguishable participation can be unidentifiable, and inferred assignments do not establish actual authorship contributions or expertise.

Topic and author probability vectors are conditionally independent given assignments under the conjugate construction, but their marginal posterior is generally coupled. The product of separate marginal posterior factors displayed in Equation (8) must not be taken as a general exact factorization. Reported prediction averages plug-in conditional means, which need not equal integrated multiword probabilities.

The historical held-out NIPS split ensures test authors already occur in training and can incorporate observed words from each test document. It does not demonstrate cold-start prediction for unseen authors. LDA overtakes the author-topic model in reported settings as more document words become available; no blanket superiority is asserted.

Symmetric-KL author similarity and topic entropy are descriptive applications. They do not validate reviewer selection, establish causal collaboration or supply calibrated measures of author competence. Finite Gibbs runs and restarts do not prove mixing, and no author software or benchmark was executed.

claims.statement: For fixed topic count T, draw each author topic vector theta_a from a symmetric Dirichlet(alpha) and each topic word vector phi_t from a symmetric Dirichlet(beta). Given a nonempty observed author set A_d, each token draws x uniformly from A_d, z from theta_x, and w from phi_z. Conditional on theta, the document-topic mixture is the arithmetic mean of its authors' topic vectors. Ordinary smoothed LDA is recovered when every document is assigned its own distinct single author and the priors match; sharing one author across documents instead pools their proportions. The author-word model requires deterministic unique topic assignment per author, a constrained degenerate case rather than a typical positive-Dirichlet draw.

claims.statement: The published Gibbs sampler jointly updates each token's author-topic pair after integrating theta and phi. For observed word v, eligible author a in A_d and topic t, the conditional weight is proportional to (n_vt^(-i)+beta)/(n_.t^(-i)+V*beta) times (n_at^(-i)+alpha)/(n_a.^(-i)+T*alpha). Counts exclude the current token; assignments outside A_d have zero weight. The uniform author-selection factor is constant among eligible pairs and cancels in normalization. Dirichlet posterior means conditional on sampled assignments estimate the author-topic and topic-word vectors; averaging across sampled assignments approximates marginal inference. Finite sampling and posterior-mean plug-ins are not exact multiword posterior predictive integration.

native_neighbors.definition: A generative message model with a topic distribution for each ordered sender-recipient pair, in which each word selects a recipient uniformly from the message's observed recipient set, a topic from that pair, and a word from the selected topic.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: Scoped to McCallum, Corrada-Emmanuel and Wang's ART model in the December 2004 technical report and IJCAI 2005 paper. Sender and recipient have distinct roles in selecting a pair-specific topic vector. The model differs from author-topic modeling over undifferentiated participants, document-specific LDA, network-edge generation and the later latent-role RART variants. ART is a source acronym within this scope, not a universal expansion of that acronym. No normalized candidate identity matched all 442 pinned AIO IDs, labels and scoped synonyms or 426 preceding native IDs, names and aliases. Both full-checkout searches included ignored and hidden files; 13 matching lines in each checkout came from four unique file contents containing prior frontier leads, contextual distinctions and a cached bibliography mention. Matching concept excerpts were inspected; the long cached web transcript was not reread in full. Semantic search returned 204 label/synonym hits: 200 verified unchanged from prior reading and four newly read. Eighteen annotated AIO CLASS nodes and outgoing edges comprise 16 verified unchanged and two newly read; 30 contextual YAMLs comprise 25 unchanged prior readings, two newly read AIO records and three final records verified against the round101 scientific-review inputs. No candidate identity is present within this bounded pinned-snapshot and maintained-corpus search.
limitations: The corpus-probability display on report p.4 factors separately integrated document marginals despite shared random parameters. The subsequent corpus-count derivation on p.5 preserves sharing. The record uses the shared model and qualifies that display; no failure of unseen implementation is inferred.

Pair-specific parameters can be weakly informed for sparse or unobserved pairs. Fixed topic count, uniform recipient selection, stationary pair preferences, finite vocabulary and bag-of-words emissions constrain the model. Suggestions to smooth toward sender-only vectors are not part of the basic specification.

Reported role similarities use descriptive topic distributions, divergence matrices and selected email examples with manual entity resolution and heuristic text cleaning. They do not establish universal predictive superiority, actual job roles, expertise or causal social relationships. Topic and role labels remain interpretations.

RART introduces additional latent sender/recipient roles and has token-level and message-level variants. It is a distinct extension; preliminary staged fitting after fixing an ART sample is not full joint posterior inference. No author code, email corpus or benchmark was executed.

native_neighbors.name: Mixed-membership model for scientific publications
native_neighbors.definition: A generative document model in which one Dirichlet-distributed membership vector mixes aspect-specific word distributions for an abstract and aspect-specific reference distributions for its bibliography.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: Scoped to the word/reference multinomial model fitted by Erosheva, Fienberg and Lafferty in their 2004 scientific-publication study. The broader mixed-membership framework and proposed Bernoulli citation alternatives are not exact aliases for this selected model. Shared document memberships couple two observation channels; no word-to-reference alignment, author identity or latent network-block membership is assumed. No normalized candidate identity matched all 442 pinned AIO IDs, labels and scoped synonyms or 426 preceding native IDs, names and aliases. Both full-checkout searches included ignored and hidden files; 13 matching lines in each checkout came from four unique file contents containing prior frontier leads, contextual distinctions and a cached bibliography mention. Matching concept excerpts were inspected; the long cached web transcript was not reread in full. Semantic search returned 204 label/synonym hits: 200 verified unchanged from prior reading and four newly read. Eighteen annotated AIO CLASS nodes and outgoing edges comprise 16 verified unchanged and two newly read; 30 contextual YAMLs comprise 25 unchanged prior readings, two newly read AIO records and three final records verified against the round101 scientific-review inputs. No candidate identity is present within this bounded pinned-snapshot and maintained-corpus search.
limitations: The main model treats references as multinomial draws with replacement although observed bibliographies are represented by presence indicators. Bernoulli inclusion models that use absent references and publication-time restrictions are discussed on pp.4-5 as alternatives; they are not the fitted multinomial model.

The p.4 display labels its integrated document likelihood p(theta|d), but it is not a posterior over parameters. Conditional independence given memberships is stronger than exchangeability alone. Shared latent proportions explain modeled dependence, not causal citation relationships or objectively true scientific disciplines.

Reported results concern a selected PNAS Biological Sciences 1997-2001 corpus and a chosen eight-aspect fit. Topic counts were compared informally, and aspect interpretations used high-probability words/references. Neither universal model-selection optimality nor recovery of a unique semantic partition follows.

An unweighted average of document loadings does not generally equal a pooled token-level percentage when document lengths differ. Source figure cross-references are inconsistent: use the actual Figure 1 on preprint p.9 and Table 4 on p.13. No source implementation or benchmark was executed.

claims.statement: For fixed K aspects, each aspect has a categorical word distribution and a separate categorical reference-ID distribution. Each document draws lambda from Dirichlet(alpha). Conditional on lambda, its word tokens are sampled from the lambda-weighted word mixture and its reference entries from the lambda-weighted reference mixture, with channel lengths conditioned on. Equivalently, each word or reference draws its own aspect label from the same lambda. The document likelihood integrates the product of both channel likelihoods over lambda; their conditional independence does not imply marginal independence. Removing the reference observations yields a word-only LDA-type model, whereas fixed rather than random membership vectors give a PLSA-style alternative.

native_neighbors.name: Gibbs sampling
native_neighbors.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that repeatedly draws a coordinate or block from its full conditional distribution given the current values of the remaining coordinates.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record denotes exact conditional resampling, including fixed coordinate cycles and fixed random-scan mixtures. It is a sampling procedure, not a Gibbs distribution, Markov random field, annealing schedule or conditional maximization method. Metropolis-within-Gibbs replaces some exact conditional draws by invariant transitions and is represented separately. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 159 prior native IDs/names/aliases. Ignored-inclusive full-checkout searches found prior discovery leads for Gibbs and slice sampling plus unrelated environment substring hits, not existing concept records. Existing HMM/MRF models and general Metropolis–Hastings were inspected to distinguish model, general transition and specialized algorithm scope.
limitations: The full conditional distributions must be compatible with a proper joint target and be sampled correctly. An approximate conditional draw is not automatically an exact Gibbs step.
Target invariance alone does not establish irreducibility, aperiodicity, convergence from every start or rapid mixing. Coordinate dependence and disconnected support can obstruct exploration.

The finite positive-state convergence theorem in Geman and Geman has explicit site-visit and positivity assumptions; it is not a theorem for every continuous, constrained or parallel Gibbs implementation.
Simultaneously updating dependent coordinates using stale neighbors is outside the stated sequential mechanism; valid parallel or adaptive scan schemes need separate arguments.
Fixed-temperature posterior sampling and a cooling schedule for optimization are different procedures. No universal convergence rate or image-restoration performance is asserted.

native_neighbors.name: Hierarchical mixture of experts
native_neighbors.definition: A conditional mixture-model family that organizes output experts as leaves of a tree and forms each leaf’s mixture weight by multiplying input-dependent probabilistic gates along its root-to-leaf path.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: The inspected Jordan–Jacobs construction uses generalized-linear experts and softmax gates with shared external input, with a finite tree defining nested soft partitions. It is static conditional modeling, distinct from temporal hidden Markov decision trees, hard classification trees, hierarchical clustering and language-specific sparse MoE routing. A mixture density network shares conditional-mixture semantics but need not impose this tree factorization or generalized-linear leaf structure. Flattening a fixed tree gives leaf weights without making every flat gating parameterization the same hierarchical model. EM, IRLS and the online surrogate are fitting procedures, not the model identity. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 382 preceding native IDs/names/aliases for the four researched candidates. Both full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files, with 45 and 45 matching lines. All 31 unique matched contents were read: prior specialized inference records, source/review context and pending leads, not exact records for the three new identities. Expanded titles, source IDs, plural forms and complete/partial-factorizability terminology were included. All 68 semantic label/synonym hits and 23 exact fully annotated AIO CLASS nodes with outgoing edges were read. Their generated YAMLs and seven native neighbors were read or byte-verified unchanged after prior complete reading, totaling 30 contextual records. The broader phrase structured variational inference is searched but not asserted as an unconditional alias of structured mean field. Boltzmann trees remains an unresolved full-text lead. Absence is bounded to the pinned vocabulary and inspected neighborhood.
limitations: The source uses soft gates that mix expert densities; it does not require hard routing, top-k sparse activation, a language model or a causal interpretation of the decision hierarchy.

Exact EM likelihood monotonicity requires a valid E-step and an M-step that increases the expected complete log likelihood under suitable regularity. It does not automatically apply to arbitrary gradient steps, the log-target least-squares surrogate or discounted online updates, and does not guarantee a global optimum.

The logistic expert output is a Bernoulli probability, not log odds; printed p.184 is qualified by the explicit Bernoulli density on p.188. In Appendix B, the multinomial total is m=sum_i y_i; displayed n factors in Equation (6.2) and the following mean/log-partition expressions cannot be copied when n denotes the number of categories.

Near-uniform gates average expert predictions, but a mixture of distinct expert densities need not become one generalized-linear density. Finite log-responsibility targets also require nonzero responsibilities.

The robot simulation uses test-error stopping and selected successful comparison runs. No unbiased generalization comparison, universal performance advantage, author-code execution or benchmark reproduction is asserted.

claims.statement: For input x and leaf l, define w_l(x) as the product of normalized child-gate probabilities along the path to l. Then p(y|x)=sum_l w_l(x) p_l(y|x). In the two-level presentation, p(y|x)=sum_i g_i(x) sum_j g_(j|i)(x) p_ij(y|x), with softmax gates and generalized-linear conditional expert densities. The conditional output mean is the corresponding weighted sum of expert means. Given an observed y, leaf responsibilities are proportional to w_l(x) p_l(y|x); they condition on both x and y, unlike input-only gates. Conditional EM alternates these responsibilities with weighted expert fits and gate fits to soft multinomial targets; a lower gate’s objective is weighted by the posterior probability of reaching its parent. The paper uses IRLS inside those maximum-likelihood subproblems. Its separate Algorithm 2 instead regresses log responsibilities by least squares, and its online variant uses discounted recursive weighted least squares. Those surrogate procedures are approximations to the specified fitting approach.

curator_calculation.interpretation: A two-token RART1 enumeration compares 512 local conditional distributions with exact integrated assignment weights over 256 states, including the same actor as sender and recipient. Shared uniform actor-role draws agree with probability 2/3, versus 1/2 for independent actors. A Beta(2,2) label mixture gives an integrated two-word probability 0.3 versus prior-mode substitution 0.25. Additive pseudocount estimates differ from flat-Dirichlet MAP. One ordinary beta=1 weighted-channel EM step increases its normalized objective only after categorical emission normalization; this finite witness does not certify the tempered experimental schedule. No source implementation or benchmark was executed.
